audit.why: Rumble 50.74% over 1285 games — a true coinflip lane, and the chart (Skill/Jax/Jax/Skill/Jax/Jax/Skill) reflects a lane Jax edges in raw duelling while Rumble owns the map. No change needed.
Counter Strike at 2-3, The Equalizer at 6, Trinity Force first item, evening out at two items — all four spikes land on the right timings.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says Counter Strike lets him 'dodge your Flamespitter damage', and the 'early' text claims harpoons fired into an active Counter Strike 'are dodged'.
audit.why: Counter Strike dodges incoming ATTACKS — basic attacks. Flamespitter is a spell and Electro Harpoon is a spell projectile; neither is dodged. The full layer already states this correctly ('Dodges autos — NOT your flamespitter'), so the two layers directly contradict each other and the content layer teaches the player to hold their strongest button for no reason.
audit.corrected: Poke straight through Counter Strike with Q and E; only stop auto-attacking.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called 'Grandmaster's Might' twice.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon names it Grandmaster-at-Arms. The old name is a fabrication on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number anywhere for Counter Strike.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 — by far the longest cooldown either champion has in lane, and the window right after it drops is when a Danger Zone Flamespitter actually wins the trade.
audit.corrected: Quote 17s and key the commit to it.

edits.before: Jax's Counter Strike (E) comes fully online — he can dodge your Flamespitter autos and stun you out of a Danger Zone trade, punishing your Heat commitment hard.
edits.after: Counter Strike comes online, but it dodges basic attacks only — Flamespitter and Electro Harpoon burn through it. The stun at the end punishes you, not lost damage.

edits.before: Double-cast Electro-Harpoon to slow him out of his Counter Strike window before he can stun you
edits.after: Double-cast Electro Harpoon into an active Counter Strike — spells are never dodged by it

edits.before: Drop Equalizer on the path between him and you whenever he runs up for an all-in to negate his gap-close
edits.after: Drop The Equalizer between you whenever he steps up, so his Leap Strike has to cross the burn to reach you

edits.before: Leap Strike onto you and immediately pop Counter Strike to dodge Flamespitter damage and stun you
edits.after: Leap Strike off a minion onto you, then Counter Strike to eat your autos and stun you inside your own cone

edits.before: Stack Trinity Force and use Grandmaster's Might passive to out-stat your frontloaded magic burst at items
edits.after: Stack Trinity Force and use Grandmaster-at-Arms' resistances to out-stat your frontloaded magic burst

edits.before: Both kits are live but neither can cleanly all-in: your Electro-Harpoon slows his chase and his Counter Strike negates your auto portion, producing a genuine skill-expression standoff.
edits.after: Neither can cleanly all-in: Counter Strike eats your autos but nothing else, and at 17 seconds on rank 1 it is the longest cooldown in the lane — the moment it ends is your window.

edits.before: Equalizer shifts your threat to the map rather than the 1v1, but Grandmaster's Might at 6 means he wins extended duels if you let him auto freely — neither side cleanly owns the window.
edits.after: The Equalizer shifts your threat to the map rather than the 1v1, but Grandmaster-at-Arms at 6 hands him every extended duel where he autos freely — neither side cleanly owns the window.

edits.before: Level 1 is a feeling-out game — Q at max cone range to chip him without committing your Heat, and respect that Jax can Leap Strike onto you the moment he hits 2 if you're standing at the tip of a short wave. Don't blow Heat recklessly; arriving at level 2 with a near-full bar means you can open with an empowered Flamespitter immediately. At level 3 he has full kit and Counter Strike, so your trade pattern becomes: Q to bait his E, then double-cast Electro-Harpoon the instant he pops it — he cannot dodge projectiles during the stun animation, but if you fire harpoons INTO an active Counter Strike they are dodged. Never auto-attack him during Counter Strike; the stun will lock you into a Danger Zone window you cannot walk out of.
edits.after: Level 1 is a feeling-out game — Q at max cone range to chip him without committing your Heat, and respect that Leap Strike can target a minion to reach you the moment he hits 2. Don't blow Heat recklessly; arriving at level 2 with a near-full bar means you can open with an empowered Flamespitter immediately. At level 3 Counter Strike is up, and the one thing to get right is what it actually stops: basic attacks. Flamespitter keeps burning and both Electro Harpoons still land through it, so keep casting and only stop auto-attacking — holding your spells for it is free damage handed back. Then walk out of the 300-range circle before it expires, because the stun, not the damage he dodges, is what actually costs you the trade.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a genuine tug-of-war. Your Danger Zone Flamespitter genuinely hurts him in short trades, but his Counter Strike still nullifies the auto-attack portion and his Leap Strike makes the gap-close instant. The winning pattern is: keep the wave slow-pushed toward his tower so he must stand in your Q cone to CS, charge your Heat naturally off minions, then hit Electro-Harpoon twice to cripple his escape when you have Danger Zone. At level 6, Equalizer changes your threat profile entirely — even if you are even on gold, the threat of a line rocket dropped the moment he commits to an all-in is a genuine deterrent. Use it to disengage a losing duel, not just to kill; a well-placed Equalizer on the river entrance also turns any skirmish with your jungler into a free kill window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a genuine tug-of-war. Danger Zone Flamespitter hurts him in short trades and Counter Strike removes only the auto portion of your damage, but Leap Strike makes his gap-close instant off any minion near you. The winning pattern is: keep the wave slow-pushed toward his tower so he must stand in your Q cone to CS, charge your Heat naturally off minions, then double Electro Harpoon to cripple his escape once you are in Danger Zone. Counter Strike is 17 seconds at rank 1, so the trade you actually commit to is the one that starts the moment it expires. At level 6 The Equalizer changes your threat profile entirely: use it to break a losing duel rather than to kill, and dropped on the river entrance it turns any skirmish with your jungler into a free kill window.

notes: The content and full layers contradicted each other on the matchup's defining interaction — the full layer already says Counter Strike dodges autos and not Flamespitter, while the content layer told the player their harpoons get dodged. Content now matches the truth. 'Grandmaster's Might' is a fabricated/legacy name; Riot's is Grandmaster-at-Arms. Two derived-flag misfires ignored rather than propagated: _missing-interactions claims Rumble's Scrap Shield and The Equalizer 'shut off Jax's Leap Strike' — Scrap Shield is a shield plus move speed with no terrain component, and The Equalizer is a damage/slow zone, not a wall, so neither actually denies a dash. Jax's Empower is also flagged 'dash' in the kit file; Riot's description is an on-next-attack buff with no dash.
